narrative.northStar: The Palawan map and travel notebook
narrative.overview:
The existing Unlock Paradise Palawan map, immersive destination photographs and original Outfit lettering define the visual world. Planning feels like arranging stops on a travel notebook alongside a satellite map. Destination guides use an editorial reading column and an ordered journey from city to shore.

Photography and maps carry expression. Home and merchandise support discovery; destination guides support reading; member planning and Admin Studio support tasks. Forms, tables, permissions and confirmations stay familiar and legible. Admin extends this same identity with a navy navigation rail, calm working surfaces and the existing official palm-lock mark.
keyCharacteristics: Existing Palawan photography, maps and official identity assets.
Outfit headings with Open Sans controls and data.
Navy, teal and gold public surfaces; scoped navy and warm sand admin themes.
Shared card anatomy, clear action boundaries and measured travel feedback.

rules.name: The Scoped Theme Rule
rules.body: Admin defaults to dark navy and offers a persistent warm light option only within the admin scope. Public pages and public-style admin Place previews retain their established palette.

rules.name: The One Heading Family Rule
rules.body: New store and admin headings inherit Outfit from their shared owner; Georgia stays with the established destination editorial material.

rules.name: The Shared Card Anatomy Rule
rules.body: Use the shared inset, compact and gap tokens for card content. Destination bodies and featured card bodies use the shared inset; Featured Destination cards navigate to the Place and do not offer an itinerary action. Product text and purchase controls are separate semantic siblings; names wrap naturally. The compact step is part of the authored scale, not a blanket override of every card.

rules.name: The Fixed Dock Rule
rules.body: Bucketlist/cart controls stay at the bottom-right viewport edge: 24px on desktop, 16px below 800px, with safe-area allowances. FloatingDock portals both controls to the body so page transforms cannot change their containing block. They never move or disappear in response to nearby page content. Shared CSS reserves final page clearance and scroll padding; map zoom controls clear the dock and failure text occupies its own row with the retry action on the left. Existing mobile field-focus, open-dialog and route exclusions remain; completing an action returns the dock to the same corner. Flights measure the actual dock, with a bottom-right transform origin for its brief confirmation pulse. This supersedes the former content-measured dock movement rule.

rules.name: The Browsing Navigation Rule
rules.body: The public brand header orders About, Membership, Merch, Contact Us, Itinerary Planner and Profile. Desktop Profile is a native disclosure with sign-in/register links for guests and the account menu for members; mobile exposes those account links directly in the left drawer. Native disclosure supports click, keyboard, Escape and outside dismissal. Area/category navigation retains the selected area. Real destination cards link to Places; protected save and itinerary controls remain separate actions. Merchandise has one floating cart with its browser-local count and no duplicate breadcrumb cart.

rules.name: The Confirmed Travel Rule
rules.body: Launch a Bucketlist plane only after the existing mutation confirms success; cart travel follows a validated browser-local addition. Flights decorate the actual state and counts, never manufacture them.

rules.name: The Consented Identity Rule
rules.body: Public traveler badges appear only after explicit sharing consent. A teal traveler-type badge leads up to two muted interest badges; private answers remain in the owner's account. Badge groups wrap naturally and keep readable labels. The account sharing checkbox shows its pending choice while disabled, announces saving, and restores the confirmed choice on failure.

rules.name: The Branded Auth Rule
rules.body: The sign-in, register and recovery forms share a branded navy form surface with the official palm-lock mark, Outfit headings, Open Sans fields and the established teal links. Field and autofill text use --p2-text. Password visibility is an inset eye icon with an accessible action name. Registration includes confirmation and a visible twelve-character minimum; both the form and server validate matching passwords.

rules.name: The Product Selection Rule
rules.body: Brand → Collection → Products is the durable catalog hierarchy. Admin selects existing categories, colors, sizes, brands and collections; an adjacent inline Add action creates a reusable option without leaving the product form. The product editor groups Product details, Photos, Options & pricing, Advanced and Publish in document flow. Photos belong to the current editor: upload/add, preview, make cover, reorder, replace and remove. There is no cross-product media picker. Upload feedback stays inline, successful partial uploads remain attached, and save is disabled while uploading. Slugs and SKUs are suggested but editable.

rules.name: The Access Point Rule
rules.body: Multiple verified access points remain separate from destination coordinates and protected by Place membership rules. Teal square pins and transport icons distinguish them from the gold destination pin. Marker names appear on hover, keyboard focus or touch selection, with an accessible name always available. Text access lists survive map failure; their named Maps actions use each access point, while the Destination section owns destination coordinates, copy and its own Maps action. Raw coordinates are omitted from the jump-off list. Place area/category/facility selection retains native add-option controls with removable selected values; access colors remain owned by --p2-teal and --p2-on-teal.

rules.name: The Dedicated Discovery Rule
rules.body: Explore options opens `/itineraries/explore/` with the selected owned trip/day. Categories, filters and photographic cards stay in normal page flow, with a prominent View final itinerary return action. My route remains the saved-stop map. Additions become Added only after the owner/version-checked mutation returns; failed additions retain the form and offer reload of the saved itinerary.

rules.name: The Public Preview Rule
rules.body: Published premium cover previews are deliberately bounded, re-encoded images addressed by opaque Place ID. Only explicit editorial Featured cards disclose a premium title; other locked cards retain generic text. Compact destination and feature hooks use the official padlock identity and task-specific copy. Upgrade opens Membership with a safe return target; Back uses a normalized internal browsing target or the homepage map.

rules.name: The Inclusive Trip Rule
rules.body: Trip creation uses start/end dates and an inclusive derived duration. An undated new trip starts with one day. Add day remains in the planner and extends a dated trip’s end date; occupied days cannot be removed by shortening dates. Profile/navigation, photos and native choices retain the shared validation, focus and theme contracts.

dos: **Do** keep the map, real photography and official palm-lock identity central to discovery.
**Do** reuse the shared state, form, tooltip, modal, card and travel owners across screens.
**Do** keep admin themes scoped and propagate the chosen theme through portals and native controls.
**Do** preserve membership, variant, quantity and owner isolation at their authoritative boundaries.
**Do** preserve visible text and control geometry throughout navigation and saves.
donts: **Don't** replace the established public palette or fonts while extending admin or merchandise.
**Don't** turn legacy generic travel time into a boat or hike duration.
**Don't** claim purchases, saves or plans succeeded before their real storage confirms them.
**Don't** aim decorative travel at a hardcoded viewport corner or cover active controls with a floating dock.
**Don't** turn inherited decorative eyebrows or glyph placeholders into reusable system rules.
